findings.title: Update invalidation compares an organization-aware wrapped model against a raw model
findings.body: update() obtains the original via getById(), which returns createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel(): for an IdP linked to an organization its isEnabled() is overridden to also require the organization (and the organization feature) to be enabled. registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate() then evaluates getLoginPredicate() on that wrapped original but on the raw updated model, while the JPA getForLogin query that populated the cache filters on the raw enabled flag. Example: an enabled, public IdP of a disabled organization is in the cached login list (raw enabled=true), but the wrapped original reports isEnabled()=false; disabling the IdP (updated enabled=false) makes both predicates false, so no login-cache invalidation is registered and the stale internal id remains in the cached getForLogin result, violating the contract that getForLogin returns only enabled login IdPs.

findings.title: Shared getLoginPredicate() semantics changed to exclude private organization brokers
findings.body: LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate() is a public SPI predicate previously defined purely by the LoginFilter values (enabled, not link-only, not hidden on login, matching getLoginSearchOptions()). This change additionally requires any organization-linked IdP to have kc.org.broker.public=true. That silently changes the meaning for every existing caller of the predicate, not just the new cache-invalidation code: a private organization broker that is legitimately usable once its organization is known (e.g. after organization identification) is now classified as never available for login, and the predicate no longer corresponds to the LoginFilter enum documented as containing all fields considered for login availability. The broker-public check should be local to the cache-invalidation decision instead of redefining the shared predicate.

findings.title: Test cleanup registers removal of a literal "alias" instead of the created IdPs
findings.body: In testCacheIDPForLogin the loop creates IdPs with aliases idp-alias-0..19 (and later idp-alias-20 at line 425) but registers cleanup as testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove, i.e. for an IdP literally named "alias" rather than the loop variable alias / the created alias. The created providers are therefore not removed (and removing the non-existent "alias" can itself fail during cleanup), leaving 21 extra IdPs in the shared test realm that can leak into other test methods of the class and make count-based cache assertions order-dependent and flaky.
